course.title: FastAPI — From Beginner to Professional
course.description: A visual-first, draft curriculum that follows the supplied 39-page FastAPI syllabus from first endpoint to secure database-backed services, testing, operations and a production-ready e-commerce capstone. Topic names and ordering are preserved; explanations, checks and diagrams are original course-authoring material.
course.version_scope: Assume Python 3.10+ and Pydantic v2-style examples. FastAPI APIs and dependencies can evolve; check installed versions and the official documentation before publishing. Lifespan context managers are preferred over deprecated on_event handlers; fastapi dev is development-only, while production run/deployment settings depend on the hosting platform. Version assumptions are advisory, not a pinned dependency lock.
audience: Python learners building their first backend API
Full-stack and mobile developers integrating HTTP APIs
Backend engineers learning testing, security and production operations
Developers building data- or AI-powered APIs
prerequisites: Basic Python syntax, variables, functions, collections, modules and exceptions. Type hints, HTTP, JSON, asynchronous programming and databases are taught or refreshed as needed.
Install a compatible Python version and work in a local virtual environment. Use synthetic data and non-production credentials for labs.
course.estimated_duration: Approximately 8–14 weeks at 6–10 hours per week, matching the attached FastAPI.pdf estimate; actual pace varies with prior Python and database experience.
learning_outcomes: Design and build FastAPI endpoints with clear HTTP semantics and typed request/response models.
Validate input, handle errors, organize application code and use dependency injection.
Integrate relational storage, migrations, authentication, authorization and external services safely.
Build asynchronous and real-time endpoints where appropriate, without confusing async with CPU speed or durability.
Write automated tests, apply security controls, observe services and prepare reliable deployments.

sections_reviewed: B: all 22 modules, 144 numbered lessons and listed subtopics
D: ten projects plus e-commerce capstone
E: advanced and specialized topic tracks
F: learning stages and prerequisite relationships
source_pdf.source_note: The full 39-page PDF was text-extracted and rendered for visual inspection. Lesson/module titles, order and subtopic coverage come from Section B; practical tasks and project objectives map to Sections C and D. Page layout artifacts and illustrative vendor logos/labels were not copied into the course. No standalone syllabus topic was intentionally excluded; advanced specialist topics are organized as optional tracks.
